text: Now a year has more than a thousand days in it.
At a six hour day, a year holds about fourteen hundred and sixty days.
By the end, over six thousand, with a sunrise every eighty-four minutes, and you'd be asked to sleep eight times a day.
At the poles the ground only turns on the spot, so people there would weigh the same as ever.
At forty-five degrees north you move at seventy percent of the equator's speed, and the push outward is half as strong.
The farther from the equator, the longer you keep your weight.
But the water leaves the poles first, so the stillest place on Earth would stand high and dry.
And the day keeps getting shorter.
